answers: Business impact from security issues within your organisation
Outages on GitHub.com affecting core Git functionality

cards.question: Which of the following is a key benefit of using GitHub Marketplace Apps in an enterprise?

options.text: They guarantee no downtime during enterprise GitHub maintenance windows
They often include integrations with external services, reducing the need for custom code
Apps eliminate the need for GitHub Actions entirely
All apps come pre-approved by GitHub’s internal security team

answers: They often include integrations with external services, reducing the need for custom code
cards.explanation: GitHub Marketplace Apps come with built-in integrations to external services - so you can plug in things like CI servers, code-quality scanners, or deployment tools without writing and maintaining custom connectors.

cards.question: You need to create a support bundle for your GitHub Enterprise Server instance with the hostname ghe.avocado.corp. What command should you use to create a support bundle?

options.text: A custom GitHub Action in the root repo
Administrator SSH access to the appliance

answers: Administrator SSH access to the appliance

cards.question: A financial services company is evaluating GitHub account types. Which of the following is a key distinction between GitHub Enterprise Managed Users and Personal Accounts?

options.text: Enterprise Managed Users can collaborate across both personal and enterprise repositories
Personal Accounts are owned by users and can be used for both personal and professional work
Personal Accounts provide stricter control over repositories and user activity
Enterprise Managed Users require the organization to manage their own authentication server

answers: Personal Accounts are owned by users and can be used for both personal and professional work

cards.question: Which THREE of the following accurately describe how the SCIM protocol enhances user management in GitHub Enterprise Cloud?

options.text: SCIM synchronizes changes to user attributes from the identity provider to GitHub
SCIM deactivates GitHub accounts when users are deleted from the identity provider.
SCIM automatically deletes organization repositories when administrators are removed.
SCIM automates user provisioning when new users are added to the identity provider.
SCIM generates authentication tokens for accessing GitHub's REST API.
SCIM configures repository permissions based on user roles within the organization.

answers: SCIM synchronizes changes to user attributes from the identity provider to GitHub
SCIM deactivates GitHub accounts when users are deleted from the identity provider.
SCIM automates user provisioning when new users are added to the identity provider.
cards.explanation: SCIM automatically updates a user's account on GitHub whenever their profile attributes change in the identity provider. When a user is removed or deacticated in IdP, SCIM deactivates (soft provisions) their GitHub account and disables access. SCIM provisions new GitHub Enterprise Cloud accounts automatically when users are added in the identity provider

cards.question: When comparing a partner identity provider integration with a non-partner identity management solution for GitHub Enterprise Managed Users, which statement is Correct?

options.text: The non-partner identity provider integrations can utilize OIDC for authentication
The non-partner identity provider integrations require manual configuration of SAML 2.0 details.
The partner identity provider integrations support fewer GitHub-supported authentication methods
The partner identity provider integrations rely on the partner to support the application on the partner IdP

answers: The non-partner identity provider integrations require manual configuration of SAML 2.0 details.
cards.explanation: Non-partner identity provider integrations require you to enter SAML2.0 configuration details by hand - such as the Sign-on URL, Issuer, and X.509 certificate - whereas partner IdPs supply a pre-configured application integration

cards.question: When comparing Group SCIM to Team Sync for identity management in GitHub Enterprise, which statement is correct?

options.text: Group SCIM requires less initial configuration than Team Sync
Team Sync supports more identity providers than Group SCIM
Team Sync provides more automated user deprovisioning than Group SCIM
Group SCIM enables centralized user and group management through the IdP

answers: Group SCIM enables centralized user and group management through the IdP
cards.explanation: GroupSCIM lets you manage both user accounts and group memberships centrally in your identity provider - automatically provisioning, updating and deplovisioning users and groups in GitHub - whereas TeamSync only mirror IdP group membership into existing GitHub teams.

cards.question: Why is a GitHub app preferred over a PAT for machine authentication?

options.text: GitHub Apps are required to pass SAML assertions
GitHub App have time-limited installation tokens with scoped access
PATs cannot be used in GitHub Actions
PATs support fewer GitHub APIs than Apps

answers: GitHub App have time-limited installation tokens with scoped access

cards.question: You are planning GitHub account management for a healthcare organization with strict compliance requirements. Which THREE of the following statements accurately describe GitHub Enterprise Managed Users (EMU) accounts?

options.text: EMU accounts can be used for both personal and enterprise repositories
EMU accounts are managed through an identity provider such as Azure AD
EMU accounts allow users to create and manage their own credentials
EMU accounts restrict users to enterprise-related activities only
EMU accounts are created and managed by individual users
EMU accounts are owned by the organization and cannot be unlinked

answers: EMU accounts are managed through an identity provider such as Azure AD
EMU accounts restrict users to enterprise-related activities only
EMU accounts are owned by the organization and cannot be unlinked
cards.explanation: Enterprise Manage User accounts are provisioned and authenticated exclusively through your identity provider (e.g. AzureAD), so the IdP handles their creation, attirbute updates and deprovisioning. Managed user accounts cannot create public content or interact with repositories outside your enterprise, they're confined to private and internal repos within the enterprise. EMU accounts are owned and controlled by the enterprise (via IdP) and cannot be converted into or unlinked as personal accounts outside that enterprise.

cards.question: A GitHub Enterprise administrator is planning to implement SAML SSO across their company. Which of the following correctly distinguishes enterprise-wide SAML SSO from organization-level SAML SSO?

options.text: Enterprise-wide SAML SSO requires less initial administrative overhead than organization-level implementation
Enterprise-wide SAML SSO allows different organizations to user different authentication methods
Enterprise-wide SAML SSO immediately removes users who fail to authenticate via the IdP
Enterprise-wide SAML SSO ensures users authenticate through the same IdP across all organizations

answers: Enterprise-wide SAML SSO ensures users authenticate through the same IdP across all organizations
cards.explanation: Enterprise-wide SAML SSO enforces a single IdP accross all member organizations. Its configuration overrides any per-organization SAML settings, so everyone must authenticate through the same provider

cards.question: What distinguishes Enterprise Managed Users (EMUs) from standard GitHub accounts?

options.text: EMUs are fully controlled by an IdP and cannot log in with personal credentials
EMUs can only be created using email invites
EMUs are managed in GitHub and use GitHub authentication
EMUs are only available for GitHub Enterprise Server

answers: EMUs are fully controlled by an IdP and cannot log in with personal credentials
cards.explanation: EMU accounts are provisioned and authenticated exclusively through your identity provider - users sign in via the IdP and cannot use or manage GitHub-native credentials

cards.question: Your organization is implementing team synchronization. Which of the following should you prioritize during the setup process?

options.text: Setting an infrequent sync schedule to reduce performance impact
Allowing manual updates to team memberships
Clearly define how identity provider groups will align with GitHub teams and roles

answers: Clearly define how identity provider groups will align with GitHub teams and roles
cards.explanation: Before you enable team synchonization, you should clearly define how groups in your identity provider will map to GitHub teams and roles - ensuring that when the sync runs, user land in the correct teams with the right permissions

cards.question: What makes GitHub Apps a more secure choice for automation over OAuth Apps?

GitHub Apps can only be installed by organization owners
GitHub Apps are limited to read-only access and cannot write to repositories

cards.question: Why would a GitHub App be favoured over a machine account for automation tasks?

cards.question: When comparing fine-grained Personal Access Token (PATs) with classic PATs, which of the following statements is accurate?

options.text: Fine-grained PATs automatically renew while classic PATs require manual renewal
Fine-grained PATs permissions can be scoped to specific repositories
Classic PATs offer more permission controls that fine-grained PATs
Classic PATs can be restricted to specific organizations, but fine-grained PATs cannot

answers: Fine-grained PATs permissions can be scoped to specific repositories
cards.explanation: Fine-grained personal access tokes let you scope permissions down to individual repositories, whereas classic PATs grant access across every repo the user can reach

cards.question: Which of the following is true about outside collaborators in a GitHub organization?

options.text: They are granted explicit access to specific repositories

They have access to all private repositories by default

cards.question: Which of the following is a benefit of creating a new GitHub organization?

options.text: Automatic inheritance of policies from other organizations
Clear separation of repos, projects, teams, billing, and organization-specific policies

cards.question: Which of the following is the responsibility of an Organization Owner in GitHub? (Choose three)

options.text: View and a manage organization billing information
Create repositories without approval from other members
Manage organization settings, such as configuration and default permissions

Create repositories without approval from other members

cards.question: Which of the following is a key benefit of setting default read permissions across organizations?

Adding or removing team members

cards.question: Q31. A token was used to access an organization's resource via API. What fields in the audit log help determine who used it?

The token ID, requesting IP address, and associated user

cards.question: Q35. When a token is used to perform actions across different GitHub resources, how is this reflected in audit logs?

options.text: Each API action made with the token generates a separate audit log entry

The audit log stores only the token name

cards.question: Q36. Which practice helps avoid service disruption when consuming GitHub APIs at scale?

Using multiple tokens to bypass limits

answers: Designing your application to work within GitHub's rate limits

cards.question: How is CodeQL different from other static analysis tools?
